results.name: trendlines: all six Excel types fit like numpy (polyfit / lstsq) — 120 random datasets incl. fixed intercept and poly orders 2–6; R² on the fitted scale

reader differential: every chart in 25 corpus workbooks (worksheets + chartsheets, one-cell/two-cell/absolute anchors) matches openpyxl — type, bar direction, grouping, series tx/cat/val refs, trendlines, titles, axis titles, anchor
reader semantics: Excel automatic titles, multi-paragraph rich titles, formula titles, combo/3-D notes, cached values when a reference cannot be resolved (defined names), live values otherwise
new-workbook writer: every corpus chart written by writeXlsxWorkbook is read back identically by openpyxl AND by our reader (refs, caches, titles, axis titles, grouping, anchors)
new charts made in Fusion export as real Excel charts: stacked / 100 % / hbar / doughnut / area / scatter, axis titles, poly + moving-average trendlines, legend — openpyxl reads every property back

renderer: Excel stacking semantics (negatives below zero, 100 % by Σ|v|, blanks), hbar first category at the bottom, trendline + equation + R² only on clustered charts, axis titles and doughnut hole drawn
patch writer: unchanged → original bytes; title / axis-title / grouping / anchor edits touch ONLY that chart (and drawing) part; openpyxl sees the edit and every other chart unchanged

patch writer: delete a chart (frame + rel + part + Override go, siblings stay), add a chart to a sheet WITH and WITHOUT a drawing, add a trendline, change the type (regenerated, reported), rename a referenced sheet (refs follow)
hostile packages: huge ptCount, 400 series, external / escaping relationship targets, malformed chart XML, chart-less drawings and 10 MB caches never crash the reader and stay bounded

persistence: charts with explicit series, trendlines, grouping, anchors survive Fusion workbook JSON; sanitizeCharts drops hostile fields (bad src paths, unknown kinds, oversize refs) and clamps trend order/period
